transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what finally made me come in is my eating has just gotten really off. Like, not just “I’m busy and skipped lunch” off, but some days before a shift I’ll realize all I’ve had is coffee and maybe a granola bar, and even that feels like I’m forcing it down.

I work in healthcare support, so I’m used to odd breaks and grabbing food when I can, but this feels different. I’m not trying to diet or lose weight or anything, but my scrubs have been hanging loose on me lately, like noticeably loose, and that kind of scared me. I keep thinking, okay, maybe it’s just stress or the schedule, but then another day goes by and I barely eat again. So… yeah, that’s the main thing that brings me in.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I have. It’s mostly in the mornings, honestly. I’ll wake up and before I’ve even really done anything—before I shower, before I put on my scrubs or my badge—there’s already this heavy, hollow feeling sitting there. Like the day is kind of ruined before it’s even started.

It’s hard to explain because it’s not always like I’m crying or having some big obvious breakdown. It’s more like… I open my eyes and there’s this weight, and I’m already tired of the day, already dreading it. And then I feel bad about that, because I know I’m supposed to get up and function and go to work like everybody else, but inside it just feels flat and heavy.
Have you noticed a decrease in pleasure or interest in activities that you used to enjoy, even things that would normally make you happy?

Yeah… definitely. That’s actually been one of the stranger parts, because I can sort of see the old version of me and what I would normally do, but I just don’t do it anymore.

Like I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park—not like marathon training or anything, but I’d go there and run the trails, clear my head a little, feel like I’d done something with the day. And I used to take photos too, just with my phone mostly, sometimes of the park or the light on buildings, little things like that. It sounds small, but I used to notice stuff. Now I’ll think about going and then almost immediately I’m like, “What’s the point?” And then I don’t go.

Same with chess. I used to play with friends, and even when I lost, it was still fun, you know? It gave me something to look forward to. Lately if someone asks, I either don’t answer right away or I make some excuse. I just don’t feel that pull toward it.

Most of the time I end up at home sitting there scrolling on my phone, not even enjoying what I’m looking at, or checking my budget spreadsheet over and over like that’s somehow productive. It’s not that those things make me happy. It’s more like they’re what I do when I can’t get myself to do anything else.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down and lost interest in things, or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

It’s not the first time I’ve felt low here and there, but this… this particular stretch feels more steady than anything I remember. The really consistent depression and losing interest in things kind of settled in later, and it’s been going on for about… a year and four months now, roughly.

I keep trying to place when it changed from “I’m just having a bad week” into “this is just how I am most days,” and it’s hard to pin down exactly, but yeah, around sixteen months. It didn’t feel like one dramatic switch flipped. It was more like the heaviness and the not caring about things I used to enjoy just became the background noise of my life, and then I realized it hadn’t really lifted.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep — like trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual even when you don’t feel rested?

Yeah, my sleep’s been… not great. It’s not like I’m just staying up watching TV or something and then wondering why I’m tired. I’ll get into bed, and I’m tired, but then I just lie there. My mind starts going back over work—little things from the day, stuff I said, stuff I should’ve done differently, whether I forgot something—and it kind of loops.

And then I’m also listening for noises, which sounds a little odd maybe, but I’ll notice every creak in the hallway or outside, and once I’m tuned into it, I can’t really relax. So even if I do fall asleep, it feels light, like I’m not fully out.

The worst part is I keep waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. It’s almost like my body has decided that’s when the night is over. I’ll wake up and check the time, and then I get frustrated because I know the alarm’s coming, but I can’t settle back down. I’ll lie there trying not to think about how little sleep I’m getting, which of course makes it harder to sleep. Then by the time the alarm actually goes off, I feel like I’ve already been awake for hours.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite, like a significant decrease or increase, or any unintentional weight loss or gain?

Yeah… my appetite’s been pretty messed up. I don’t know if I noticed it right away, because at first I think I told myself I was just busy or rushing in the mornings, but it’s become pretty obvious.

Some days before a shift I’ll basically only manage coffee and maybe a granola bar, and even that feels like I’m just doing it because I know I should have something in my stomach. It’s not like I’m choosing to diet or trying to eat healthier or anything. Food just doesn’t really call to me the way it used to, and then I’ll look up and realize I’ve gone most of the day barely eating.

And my scrubs have been hanging loose on me lately, which is what made it harder to ignore. I’ll tie the pants tighter or notice the top feels baggier, and it kind of hits me that I’m losing weight even though I’m not trying to. I haven’t been carefully tracking it or anything, but yeah, there’s definitely been a decrease in appetite and some weight loss that I didn’t plan.
Have you found yourself feeling more tired than usual, moving more slowly, or feeling like you're moving through something heavy? Or maybe feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah… I’ve noticed both, actually, which is kind of frustrating because it doesn’t feel consistent. At work, especially in the supply area, there are times when I’m just pacing around like I can’t settle. I’ll check the same drawers more than once, like I’m making sure things are where they’re supposed to be, but then I realize I already checked that drawer two minutes ago. It’s not even always that something needs checking right then — I just feel keyed up and I keep moving.

But other times it’s the opposite. I feel like I’m moving through wet cement or something. Simple things that should be quick take me way too long. Like drawing up labels, or answering a patient when they ask me something straightforward — I’ll hear them, but it takes me a second to get myself together and respond. It’s embarrassing because I know how to do my job, and I know these tasks shouldn’t be hard, but it’s like my body and brain are lagging.

So yeah, either I’m pacing and repeating the same checks, or I’m slowed down enough that things take twice as long as they should.
